Rashi on Shabbat 87b:1:1.hebrew: לחנייתן - שהרי בר"ח חנו, והכי קאמר: ששי לחנייתן הוא הששי בחדש, הוא ששי בשבת:
Rashi on Shabbat 87b:1:1.english: From their encampment - For they encamped on Rosh Chodesh, and this is what it is saying: the sixth [day] from their encampment — it is the sixth [day] of the month, [and] it is the sixth [day] of the week [Friday].

Rashi on Shabbat 87b:1:2.english: For their journey - [It is] also for their journey, for on the day they came to the Wilderness of Sinai, they journeyed from Rephidim.

Rashi on Shabbat 87b:1:3.hebrew: וקא מיפלגי - רב אחא ורבא במצות שבת שנאמר להם במרה, אם נצטוו על התחומין בו ביום או לא. דכתיב בדברות האחרונות "שמור את יום השבת לקדשו כאשר צוך", ש"מ קודם הדברות נצטוו בה:
Rashi on Shabbat 87b:1:3.english: And they disagree - Rav Acha and Rava [disagree] regarding the mitzvah of Shabbat that was stated to them at Marah, whether they were commanded concerning [Shabbat] boundaries on that day or not. For it is written in the latter [Ten] Commandments, "Observe the Shabbat day to keep it holy, as [He] commanded you" — learn from this [that] they were commanded concerning it prior to the [Ten] Commandments.

Rashi on Shabbat 87b:1:4.hebrew: ואר"י במרה - דכתיב שם שם לו חק ומשפט (שמות ט״ו:כ״ה):
Rashi on Shabbat 87b:1:4.english: And Rav Yehuda said: In Mara - As it is written: "There He made for him a statute and an ordinance" (Exodus 15:25).

Rashi on Shabbat 87b:1:5.hebrew: אתחומין לא איפקוד - הלכך, כשנסעו מרפידים, נסעו בשבת, שלא הוזהרו לילך יותר מאלפים אמה:
Rashi on Shabbat 87b:1:5.english: They were not commanded regarding [Shabbat] boundaries - Therefore, when they journeyed from Refidim, they journeyed on Shabbat, for they had not been warned [not] to go more than two thousand cubits.

Rashi on Shabbat 87b:2:1.english: In the evening - "In the evening" implies the following evening.

Rashi on Shabbat 87b:2:2.hebrew: ריש ירחא דאייר שבתא - שהרי ניסן מלא הוא לעולם, וריש ירחא דסיון בחד בשבתא:
Rashi on Shabbat 87b:2:2.english: The New Moon of Iyyar [was] Shabbat - For Nisan is always a full [month], and the New Moon of Sivan [was] on the first day of the week.

Rashi on Shabbat 87b:3:1.hebrew: השלים ניסן - נתמלא בשלשים יום, לשון שלם. חיסר אייר, שהרי אייר חסר כסדרן, ומתרמי סיון בחד בשבתא:
Rashi on Shabbat 87b:3:1.english: Nisan was complete - It was filled with thirty days — an expression [meaning] "complete." Iyyar was deficient, for Iyyar is deficient according to its regular order, and [thus] Sivan falls out on the first [day] of the week [Sunday].

Rashi on Shabbat 87b:5:1.hebrew: ואותו היום שבת היה שנא' ובקר וראיתם וגו' - שנתרעמו בו ביום על המן, כדכתיב: וילונו על משה וגו' להמית את כל הקהל הזה ברעב, והבטיחם להוריד להם מן למחר. וע"כ בחד בשבת ירד להם מן תחלה, שנאמר: ששת ימים תלקטוהו, וביום השביעי לירידתו שבת לא יהיה בו:
Rashi on Shabbat 87b:5:1.english: And that day was Shabbat, as it is stated: “And in the morning, then you shall see,” etc. - For on that day they complained about the manna, as it is written: “And they murmured against Moses, etc., to kill this whole assembly with hunger,” and He promised them to bring down manna for them on the morrow. Therefore, on Sunday manna first came down for them, as it is stated: “Six days you shall gather it, and on the seventh day” — [that is,] of its descent — “Sabbath, there shall be none in it.”

Rashi on Shabbat 87b:5:2.hebrew: ריש ירחא דסיון חד בשבת - כשתשלים לאייר עד ט"ו, ויום ט"ו ר"ח סיון:
Rashi on Shabbat 87b:5:2.english: The New Moon of Sivan [was on] the first [day] of the week - When you complete Iyyar up to fifteen [days], the fifteenth day [is] the New Moon of Sivan.

Rashi on Shabbat 87b:6:1.english: Ten crowns - [It was] the first of ten things.

Rashi on Shabbat 87b:6:10.hebrew: לאיסור הבמות - מעכשיו נאסרו, שהוא ראוי לפתח אהל מועד, כדכתיב "ואל פתח אהל מועד לא הביאו":
Rashi on Shabbat 87b:6:10.english: Of the prohibition of improvised altars - From now on they were prohibited, since [the offering] is fit for the entrance of the Tent of Meeting, as it is written: "and to the entrance of the Tent of Meeting he has not brought it."

Rashi on Shabbat 87b:6:11.english: Of this year - [In the] second year of their exodus, the Tabernacle was erected.

Rashi on Shabbat 87b:6:2.english: First of the creation of the world - For it was Sunday.

Rashi on Shabbat 87b:6:3.hebrew: ראשון לנשיאים - להקרבת נשיאים לחנוכת הבית:
Rashi on Shabbat 87b:6:3.english: First of the princes - For the offering of the princes for the dedication of the Tabernacle.

Rashi on Shabbat 87b:6:4.hebrew: ראשון לכהונה - אותו היום שמיני למילואים, ועבודה באהרן ובניו, ועד עכשיו היה בבכורות:
Rashi on Shabbat 87b:6:4.english: First of the priesthood - That day [was] the eighth [day] of the inauguration, and [the] service [was performed] by Aaron and his sons, whereas until now it was [performed] by the firstborn.

Rashi on Shabbat 87b:6:5.hebrew: ראשון לעבודה - לסדר עבודת ציבור, תמידין ושאר קרבנות של תרומת הלשכה:
Rashi on Shabbat 87b:6:5.english: First for service - For the order of the communal service, [namely] the daily [tamid] offerings and the other sacrifices from the chamber's appropriation.

Rashi on Shabbat 87b:6:6.english: For the descent of fire - "And fire came forth from before the Lord and consumed upon the altar," etc. (Leviticus 9:24).

Rashi on Shabbat 87b:6:7.hebrew: לאכילת קדשים - במחיצה, ועד עכשיו היו נאכלים בכל מקום:
Rashi on Shabbat 87b:6:7.english: For the eating of consecrated [foods] - Within an enclosure, whereas until now they were eaten in any place.

Rashi on Shabbat 87b:6:8.hebrew: לשכון - בישראל. שכינה שרתה שם, כדכתיב "ושכנתי בתוכם", מכלל דעד השתא לא שרתה:
Rashi on Shabbat 87b:6:8.english: To dwell - In Israel. The Divine Presence rested there, as it is written, "And I will dwell among them," which implies that until now it had not rested [there].

Rashi on Shabbat 87b:6:9.hebrew: לברך - ברכת כהנים, כדכתיב "וישא אהרן את ידיו" וגו':
Rashi on Shabbat 87b:6:9.english: To bless - [With] the Priestly Blessing, as it is written: "And Aaron lifted his hands," etc.

Rashi on Shabbat 87b:7:1.hebrew: ד' ימים - כשאתה קובע כל החדשים כסדרן, אחד מלא ואחד חסר, הוו ארבעה ימים בין תחלת שנה לתחלת שנה אחרת, שמנין חדשי לבנה כסדרן שנ"ד ימים — כולן שבועין חוץ מארבעה ימים:
Rashi on Shabbat 87b:7:1.english: Four days - When you establish all the months in their regular order — one full and one deficient — there are four days between the beginning of one year and the beginning of the next year, for the count of the lunar months in their regular order is 354 days, all of which are [complete] weeks except for four days.

Rashi on Shabbat 87b:7:2.hebrew: ואם היתה שנה מעוברת ה' - דקסבר שני האדרים עבדינן חסרים, ופסח דחוי יום אחד, לקמן:
Rashi on Shabbat 87b:7:2.english: And if it was a leap year, five [days] - Because he holds [that] we make both Adars lacking [i.e., twenty-nine days each], and Passover is pushed off by one [additional] day, [as discussed] later.

Rashi on Shabbat 87b:7:3.hebrew: ז' חסרים עבוד - ולא היו אלא ג' בין פסח לפסח, הלכך דאישתקד בה' בשבא. ולית ליה דאחרים, דאמרי: אין מעברין ואין מחסרין שום חדש לצורך, אלא לעולם אחד מלא ואחד חסר:
Rashi on Shabbat 87b:7:3.english: They established seven lacking [months] - And there were only three [days] between [one] Pesach and [the next] Pesach; therefore, [that] of the previous year [was] on Thursday. And [Rabbi Yosei] does not hold like Acherim, who say [that] we do not make any month full or lacking for a [particular] need; rather, [there is] always one full [month] and one lacking [month].

Tosafot on Shabbat 87b:1:1.hebrew: ואמר רב יהודה כאשר צוך במרה - האי קרא במשנה תורה כתיב, וליכא למימר "כאשר צוך" במתן תורה, שהרי משה לא היה מספר אלא על הסדר, ובכולהו לא כתיב "כאשר צוך":
Tosafot on Shabbat 87b:1:1.english: And Rav Yehudah said: "As He commanded you" — in Marah - This verse is written in Mishneh Torah [Deuteronomy], and one cannot say [that] "as He commanded you" [refers to] the giving of the Torah [at Sinai], for Moses was only recounting [the commandments] in order, and in all the other [commandments] "as He commanded you" is not written.

Tosafot on Shabbat 87b:1:2.hebrew: כאשר צוך במרה - ואם תאמר: מנא ליה דבמרה איפקוד אשבת? דילמא "כאשר צוך" בפרשת מן, דאשכחן דיני שבת כתובין שם: "את אשר תאפו אפו" וגו'! וי"ל: משום דבכיבוד אב ואם נמי כתיב "כאשר צוך", ומסתמא כי היכי דהאי "כאשר צוך" במרה — הכי נמי האי; וכן מוכח בפרק ד' מיתות (סנהדרין דף נו:) דאיתמר מילתיה דר' יהודה אתרווייהו. וא"ת: וכיון דבמרה איפקוד אשבת, היכי אמרינן בפ' כל כתבי (לקמן שבת קיח:): "אלמלי שמרו ישראל שבת ראשונה, לא שלטה בהן אומה ולשון, שנאמר: 'ויהי ביום השביעי יצאו מן העם ללקוט' וגו', וכתיב בתריה: 'ויבא עמלק'" — אמאי קרי להאי "שבת ראשונה", כיון דבמרה נצטוו? והא לא היתה שבת ראשונה, דמעיקרא כתיב: "ויסעו מאילם ויבאו" וגו', ואמרינן בסמוך דאותו היום שבת היה! ועוד מקשים, דמשמע מתוך הפסוקים ששתי שבתות היו קודם: ראשונה כשנסעו מאילם, ואחר אותו שבת ירד להם המן, וכתיב: "ויהי ביום הששי לקטו לחם משנה" וגו' "ויניחו אותו עד הבקר" וגו' ["ויאמר משה אכלוהו היום" וגו' "ששת ימים תלקטוהו" וגו' "ויהי ביום השביעי יצאו מן העם ללקוט" וגו'] — משמע שבשבת שלישית שאחר מרה היא:
Tosafot on Shabbat 87b:1:2.english: "As He commanded you — in Marah" - And if you will say: From where does [Rav] know that they were commanded concerning Shabbat in Marah? Perhaps "as He commanded you" [refers to the command] in the section of the manna, as we find the laws of Shabbat written there: "That which you will bake, bake, etc."! And one can say [in answer]: Because regarding honoring [one's] father and mother it is also written "as [the Lord your God] commanded you," and presumably, just as that "as He commanded you" [was given] in Marah, so too this one; and so it is proven in the chapter [entitled] Arba Mitot (Sanhedrin 56b), where Rav Yehudah's statement was stated regarding both of them. And if you will say: Since they were commanded concerning Shabbat in Marah, how do we say in the chapter [entitled] Kol Kitvei (below, Shabbat 118b): "Had Israel kept the first Shabbat, no nation or tongue would have ruled over them, as it is stated: 'And it came to pass on the seventh day that some of the people went out to gather, etc.,' and it is written afterward: 'And Amalek came'" — why does [the Gemara] call this "the first Shabbat," since they were [already] commanded [about Shabbat] in Marah? And [furthermore], this was not [even] the first Shabbat [after Marah], for earlier it is written: "And they journeyed from Elim and came, etc.," and we say nearby [in the Gemara] that that day was Shabbat! And furthermore, they ask, for it is implied from the verses that there were two Shabbats beforehand: the first when they journeyed from Elim, and after that Shabbat the manna descended for them, and it is written: "And it came to pass on the sixth day, they gathered double bread, etc.," "and they laid it up until the morning, etc." ["and Moses said: Eat it today, etc., six days you shall gather it, etc., and it came to pass on the seventh day that some of the people went out to gather, etc."] — which implies that it was on the third Shabbat after Marah:

Tosafot on Shabbat 87b:1:3.hebrew: אתחומין לא איפקוד - אין צ"ל דאתיא כר' עקיבא דאמר תחומין דאורייתא — דהא משמע לכ"ע דבסיני לכל הפחות איפקוד אתחומין — דלאו דוקא נקט תחומין, אלא כלומר הוצאה, שהיו מוליכין עמהן כל אשר להן; ומר סבר אהוצאה לא איפקוד, ומר סבר איפקוד. ואע"ג דבפרשת מן כתיב: "אל יצא איש ממקומו", ודרשינן מיניה הוצאה בספ"ק דעירובין (דף יז:) — איכא למימר שאחר מתן תורה נאמר, אחר שנעשה המשכן, [כמו] שאמר הקב"ה להניח צנצנת לפני העדות, ומשום דשייכי למילי דמן כתבינהו התם. ולמאן דאמר איפקוד — אע"פ שבמרה נאמר, כתביה התם כדפרישית:
Tosafot on Shabbat 87b:1:3.english: They were not commanded about boundaries - One does not need to say that [this] follows Rabbi Akiva, who says [that] Shabbat boundaries are biblical — since it is implied according to all opinions that at Sinai, at the very least, they were commanded regarding boundaries — for [the Gemara] did not mean boundaries literally, rather it meant carrying out [from a domain], as they were taking all that they had with them; and one Master holds [that at Marah] they were not commanded regarding carrying out, and one Master holds [that] they were commanded. And even though in the portion of the manna it is written: "Let no man go out of his place," and we derive carrying out from it at the end of the first chapter of Eruvin (17b) — one can say that it was stated after the giving of the Torah, after the Tabernacle was made, [just as] the Holy One, blessed be He, said to place a jar [of manna] before the Testimony; and because [these matters] belong to the topic of the manna, [Scripture] wrote them there. And according to the one who says they were commanded — even though it was stated at Marah, [Scripture] wrote it there, as I have explained.

Tosafot on Shabbat 87b:2:1.hebrew: ואותו יום חמישי בשבת היה כו' - ואם כן ברביעי שחטו פסחיהם, ונמצא בשבת שעברה לקחו פסחיהן, שאז היה בעשור לחדש. ועל כן קורין אותו "שבת הגדול", לפי שנעשה בו נס גדול, כדאמרינן במדרש (שמות רבה פ' בא): כשלקחו פסחיהם באותה שבת, נתקבצו בכורות אומות העולם אצל ישראל ושאלום: "למה היו עושין כך?" אמרו להן: "זבח פסח לה', שיהרוג בכורי מצרים." הלכו אצל אבותיהם ואל פרעה לבקש ממנו שישלחו ישראל, ולא רצו. ועשו בכורות מלחמה, והרגו מהן הרבה; הה"ד: "למכה מצרים בבכוריהם":
Tosafot on Shabbat 87b:2:1.english: And that day was the fifth [day] of the week, etc. - If so, on Wednesday they slaughtered their Paschal lambs, and it follows that on the previous Shabbat they took their Paschal lambs, for that was on the tenth of the month. Therefore, it is called "Shabbat HaGadol" [the Great Shabbat], because a great miracle occurred on it, as we say in the Midrash (Shemot Rabbah, Parashat Bo): When they took their Paschal lambs on that Shabbat, the firstborn of the nations of the world gathered to Israel and asked them: "Why are you doing this?" They said to them: "[It is] a Passover sacrifice to the Lord, Who will slay the firstborn of Egypt." They went to their fathers and to Pharaoh to ask him to send Israel away, but they refused. So the firstborn waged war and killed many of them; this is what is written: "To Him who struck Egypt through their firstborn" [Psalms 136:10].

Tosafot on Shabbat 87b:5:1.hebrew: וכתיב ששת ימים תלקטוהו - תימה: היכי מייתי ראיה מהאי קרא דבשבת היה? והלא זה הפסוק נכתב אחר שירד כבר מן שבוע, כשהגידו נשיאי העדה למשה שלקטו לחם משנה, דכתיב: "ויאמר משה אכלוהו היום וגו' ששת ימים תלקטוהו", והמן כבר ירד מיום ראשון שעבר! ואור"י, דאע"ג דלא נאמר עד אח"כ, מ"מ מוכח שפיר; דמשה שכח לומר להם, והיה אומר: "היה לי לומר לכם מה שאמר הקב"ה כשנתן את המן, שתלקטוהו ששת ימים", וא"כ אחד בשבת היה:
Tosafot on Shabbat 87b:5:1.english: And it is written: "Six days you shall gather it" - [This is] astonishing: how does [the Gemara] bring a proof from this verse that [that day] was Shabbat? Was this verse not written after the manna had already been falling for a week, when the leaders of the congregation told Moses that they had gathered a double portion of bread, as it is written: "And Moses said: Eat it today, etc. Six days you shall gather it," and the manna had already been falling since the previous Sunday? And R"I answers: Even though it was not stated until afterward, nevertheless it is well proven; for Moses had forgotten to tell them, and he was saying [to them]: "I should have told you what the Holy One, blessed be He, said when He gave the manna, that you shall gather it for six days," and if so, [the day the manna began falling] was Sunday.

Tosafot on Shabbat 87b:6:1.hebrew: עשר עטרות נטל אותו היום - הא דלא חשיב ראשון להקמת המשכן, משום דאמרינן במדרש (ויקרא רבה ס' סמיני) שכל ז' ימי המלואים היה משה מעמיד המשכן ומפרקו. אי נמי, משום דעליה דהקמת המשכן קאי, דה"ק: אותו היום של הקמת המשכן נטל עשר עטרות אחרות:
Tosafot on Shabbat 87b:6:1.english: That day took ten crowns - [The reason] it does not count "the first [day] of the erection of the Tabernacle" is because we say in the Midrash (Vayikra Rabbah, Shemini) that throughout all seven days of the inauguration [miluim], Moses would erect the Tabernacle and dismantle it. Alternatively, [it is] because [the statement] refers to the erection of the Tabernacle, for this is what it is saying: That day of the erection of the Tabernacle took ten other crowns.

Tosafot on Shabbat 87b:6:2.hebrew: ראשון לאכילת קדשים - ובת"כ, במקום "אכילת קדשים" קתני "שחיטתן בצפון":
Tosafot on Shabbat 87b:6:2.english: The first [time] for the eating of consecrated [offerings] - And in Torat Kohanim, instead of "the eating of consecrated [offerings]," it teaches "their slaughter in the north":
